summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for recurrent syncope associated with coughing. He presented with worsening dyspnea, weight gain to 91 kg, and signs of fluid overload. Workup revealed elevated BNP and mild pulmonary edema on imaging, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure. His syncope was evaluated with normal head CT, EKG, and telemetry; neurology attributed the episodes to cough-induced syncope. He was treated with IV diuresis, achieving a discharge weight of 84.7 kg, with improvement in symptoms and renal function (creatinine from 2.4 to 1.6). Losartan was uptitrated to 25 mg daily, and plans were made for outpatient follow-up with cardiology, pulmonology for a suspicious right upper lobe nodule, and primary care for iron deficiency anemia. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions on weight monitoring, medication adherence, and low-salt diet.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
